note: Ceilings for tests/test_contract_agent.py: tool_calls counts every MCP tool call the two scripted seats make in one run, bytes_received the UTF-8 bytes of the text content of every answer. Both are the measured values, identical over five runs, with no headroom. Raise either only with a stated reason in the same PR. F2 lowered bytes_received by 616 (from 147,207): the desk's ready-lane and not_offered meanings were shortened when they gained the review-request answer. C6 raised bytes_received by 312 (from 146,591) with the same 56 calls: each my_desk answer's office carries `fence` with the comparison basis only, +324 over 6 desk reads; the work context's how_to_claim text is shorter, -12 over 2 reads. F12 lowered bytes_received by 37,423 (25.5%, from 146,903) with the same 56 calls: every answer's text is sent as compact JSON instead of indented JSON. The whitespace removed is 44,315 bytes; the seat's my_desk reads, which the budget cut, now carry more of the desk within the same budget (+6,892 bytes as dd594b1 would have rendered them). W3 raised bytes_received with the same 56 calls: each work-context answer carries the work_order report. F8 raised bytes_received by 1,031 (from 109,686) with the same 56 calls: the lease events the two seats drain carry their generation, handoff token and verdict as fields. A12 lowered tool_calls by 1 (56 to 55) and bytes_received by 39: the seat renews on the generation alone, so it no longer re-reads the issue for an ETag; the renewal hint is longer and claim answers carry issue_etag. F11 kept tool_calls at 55 and lowered bytes_received by 1,368: a claim_held refusal is followed by one quiet wait from its events_after cursor and then claim_next_ready, where it was followed by a lease read; the holder's lease_generation_required names its generation as a field, so the renewal follows with no lease read. A13 raised bytes_received by 1,333 with the same 55 calls: expiry seconds, the empty review-request lane and the RFC 3339 timestamps in every packet the two seats read. A refusal keeps the packet conventions, which raised bytes_received by 28: the claim_held refusal Terra meets carries its expiry in the one shape with expires_in_seconds beside it. C7 raised bytes_received by 30 with the same 55 calls: the one renewal Sol makes answers with renewals_without_progress, the count a holder reads before its claim is raised. W5 raised bytes_received by 70 with the same 55 calls: the two work-context reads carry the learnings lane, empty here. G10 raised bytes_received by 240 (from 110,771) with the same 55 calls: the issue reads the two seats make carry authored_by, who wrote the issue's current text. AD8 and AD6 raised bytes_received by 792 with the same 55 calls: the work context of an issue the seat holds carries your_lease, and an open handoff carries replies posted since the yield. AD10 raised bytes_received by 416 (111,803 to 112,219): each desk read carries identity.last_run. AD9 raised bytes_received by 220 (112,219 to 112,439): the one invalid_arguments refusal now carries violations by path, an example of the argument's shape and next naming the same tool. AD2 lowered bytes_received by 28,531 (112,439 to 83,908) with the same 55 calls: my_desk and get_issue_work_context answer lean on MCP, without the fixed explanations athena://answers/glossary now holds once and without null-valued keys. AD5 raised bytes_received by 366 (83,908 to 84,274): each desk read carries the asks.questions lane. AD4 raised bytes_received by 728 (84,274 to 85,002): each desk read opens with next, its first moves. AD12's grouped desk preview lowered bytes_received by 4,741 (85,002 to 80,261): each desk read folds its notification preview one row per issue. The dogfood verdict raised bytes_received by 56 (80,261 to 80,317) with the same 55 calls: the one invalid_arguments refusal's next hint also names valid_arguments, the list an unknown argument's refusal carries now that every tool refuses an argument it does not take.
